correctness.rationale: The radical identity \(G(n)/n=G(\operatorname{rad}n)/\operatorname{rad}n+\sum_{p\mid n}(e_p-1)/p\) follows directly from the factorized arithmetic derivative and Euler product. For prime powers it gives \(G(p^e)=(e-1)p^{e-1}\), with minimum two only at \(4\). For two-prime support \(p^a q^b\), direct expansion gives \(G=p^{a-1}q^{b-1}[(a-1)q+(b-1)p+1]\), so the nonsquarefree minimum is eight only at \(12\). For a squarefree triple \(pqr\), \(G=p+q+r-1\ge9\) with equality only at \(30\); adding further squarefree primes strictly increases \(G\), while repeated exponents add a strictly positive radical term. These support bounds make the listed fibers through nine exhaustive. An independent enumeration through \(20000\) reproduced all stated minima and fibers; the proof is unrestricted.
residual_risks: The theorem determines only the first support thresholds and fibers through nine.

Its current entry proves nonnegativity and records the complete fibers \(G=0\) and \(G=1\), while its data visibly contains the early values but does not prove that no later integer enters fibers two through nine.
